note: E1 of ORD-2026-08-30-01. The expected glyph-package for each of the five conformance examples, DERIVED BY HAND from `.guidelines/PACKAGE_TARGET.md` applied to `conformance/examples.json`, never from an emitter (locks T4, T5, T31). No glyph-package emitter exists at the time of writing; that is the point. `package` is the claim, and an emitter that disagrees with it is wrong until this file is revised for a stated reason.
derivation_rules: S2: the root becomes <glyph-package engine="2.4.5.01">, unconditionally
S5: <schema/> is emitted empty as the first child of the root
S3: each maximal run of siblings starting at chain="extend" becomes a <chain>; the attribute does not survive the grouping; a run of one is still a run
S4: an element whose command is `composite` gains <invoke reads species depth/> as its FIRST child, before any <chain>; atoms gain nothing
diagnostics_are_not_in_the_document: The emitted document carries no diagnostic content and never has: a refusal reaches it as <off> (XML_REFERENCE.md 11.3) and an advisory rule diagnostic reaches it not at all. Diagnostics travel beside the document, in the AST envelope glyph-check validates. They are recorded per case here because a golden blind to them would let a regression that silences the contradiction rules pass unseen.

  <schema/>
  <block once="true">
    <instruction>
      <target>
        <user-input>phonema-orbital</user-input>
      </target>
      <rationale>
        <invoke reads="[ELAB[RSN]],[REF[CNST]]" species="composite" depth="1"/>
        <chain>
          <go/>
        </chain>
        <user-input>cover cases where 2 vowels cost -0.1 when repeated</user-input>
      </rationale>
      <note>
        <user-input>start</user-input>
      </note>
      <context>
        <chain>
          <reference/>
        </chain>
        <user-input>now: aa -> 0.9 + 0.9 | expected: aa -> 0.9 + 0.8</user-input>
      </context>
      <always force="editorial">
        <chain>
          <true/>
        </chain>
        <user-input>alphanumeric inputs in the app's CLI.</user-input>
      </always>
      <note>
        <user-input>path</user-input>
      </note>
      <instead-of>
        <chain>
          <add/>
        </chain>
        <user-input>no need to change anything besides adding this rule. try to change the code as less as possible.</user-input>
      </instead-of>
    </instruction>
  </block>
</glyph-package>
cases.roundTripNote: pinned, not a defect, and carried unchanged from examples.json: the source holds an apostrophe, and text holding an apostrophe, a backslash, a backtick or a bracket is substituted rather than preserved. The substitution reaches the document, so this pair is unstable by design. The pin is per case so a real regression cannot hide behind a known loss.

cases.note: the degenerate case for both new constructs: no chain and no invoke, so it is what proves <glyph-package> and <schema/> are unconditional (S18) rather than triggered by a feature. It is also the case that contradicts finding A1: the order records zero diagnostics across all five examples, and this one produces four at 2.4.5.01.

identity: Each case carries `digest`, the first 12 hex of sha256 over its `src`. The id E-01 is a human label; the digest is the identity. A pin carries `pinnedTo` so it binds to the SOURCE it excuses rather than to a position: a pin that migrates to another case does not outlive its reason, it acquires a false one, and lock T10 does not catch that.
engine_note: the documents were hand-derived at 2.4.5.01 and the engine attribute is the version that produced them. Bumping it here is declaring the version, not re-deriving from the emitter: every other byte is unchanged from the hand derivation.
